baseEvents.title: Daughter's Recital
baseEvents.description: Your daughter has a recital tonight, but a client also wants a late call.
baseEvents.wisdom: Kids remember who showed up. They will not remember the Q3 pipeline review. Your client will get over it. Your daughter will not forget.

choices.label: Attend the recital
choices.memory: You showed up for your daughter's recital.

choices.label: Work overtime
choices.memory: You took the overtime call and missed the recital.

choices.label: Split the evening
choices.memory: You caught part of the recital before returning to work.

baseEvents.title: Annual Checkup
baseEvents.description: Your doctor has an opening for a preventive visit, but it means taking time off work.
baseEvents.wisdom: You've been meaning to book this for 14 months. The doctor's office is starting to take it personally.

choices.label: Book the appointment
choices.memory: You made time for a preventive health checkup.

choices.label: Put it off
choices.memory: You postponed your annual checkup again.

choices.label: Use telehealth
choices.memory: You handled your checkup through a quick telehealth visit.

baseEvents.title: Weekend Getaway
baseEvents.description: Your partner suggests a low-key weekend away to reconnect.
baseEvents.wisdom: Relationships don't fail from one big fight—they fade from a thousand small moments you didn't make time for. This getaway is a chance to remember why you chose each other.

choices.label: Plan the trip
choices.memory: You planned a weekend getaway and reconnected.

choices.label: Stay home and save
choices.memory: You stayed home to protect the budget.

choices.label: Do a day trip
choices.memory: You chose a smaller day trip that still felt special.

baseEvents.title: Career Course
baseEvents.description: A practical online course could improve your future earning power.
baseEvents.wisdom: Module 1 is inspiring. Module 2 is fine. You will not finish Module 3.

choices.label: Enroll
choices.memory: You enrolled in a career course and invested in yourself.

choices.label: Keep evenings free
choices.memory: You protected your evenings instead of adding coursework.

choices.label: Audit free lessons
choices.memory: You sampled free lessons before committing.

baseEvents.title: Date Night
baseEvents.description: There is finally a free evening for your relationship.
baseEvents.wisdom: The person you chose matters. Protect time with them like you'd protect your health—because your relationship is your health. Rescheduling again is how marriages become roommates.

choices.label: Go out
choices.memory: You invested in a relaxed date night.

choices.label: Movie at home
choices.memory: You kept date night cozy at home.

choices.label: Reschedule
choices.memory: You rescheduled date night again.

baseEvents.title: Side Hustle Offer
baseEvents.description: A short freelance job could add cash but eats into family time.
baseEvents.wisdom: The client says it'll take 10 hours. It will take 35. You already know this.

choices.label: Accept it
choices.memory: You accepted a demanding side hustle.

choices.label: Negotiate scope
choices.memory: You negotiated a smaller freelance project.

choices.label: Decline
choices.memory: You declined extra work to protect home life.

baseEvents.title: Therapy Session
baseEvents.description: A therapy opening appears during a stressful stretch.
baseEvents.wisdom: You have been 'thinking about calling someone' for four months. The opening is right there.

choices.label: Take the slot
choices.memory: You used therapy to process a hard week.

choices.label: Journal instead
choices.memory: You journaled through your feelings.

choices.label: Push through
choices.memory: You pushed through stress without support.

baseEvents.title: Kids' Sports Signup
baseEvents.description: Registration opens for the season. Your child is extremely excited. You are looking at the Saturday schedule with quiet dread.
baseEvents.wisdom: Sports teaches kids things school can't: how to fail, how to try again, how to be part of a team. The cost is real, but so is what your kid learns about themselves.

choices.label: Sign up
choices.memory: You signed up for a busy sports season.

choices.label: Find scholarship
choices.memory: You searched for a scholarship to make sports possible.

choices.label: Wait a season
choices.memory: You waited on sports registration this season.

baseEvents.title: Investment Choice
baseEvents.description: You have a chance to move extra cash into savings or spend it now.
baseEvents.wisdom: Every dollar you don't invest today is a dollar that won't be there when you need it. Spending it feels good now, but it's stealing from future-you who might be in a tight spot.

choices.label: Invest extra
choices.memory: You moved extra cash toward future savings.

choices.label: Buy something fun
choices.memory: You spent extra cash on a fun purchase.

choices.label: Emergency fund
choices.memory: You strengthened the emergency fund.

baseEvents.title: Parent-Teacher Conference
baseEvents.description: The teacher asks for a conference about slipping homework and classroom focus.
baseEvents.wisdom: Ignoring problems at school doesn't make them go away—it makes them bigger. A teacher reaching out is actually them being on your team. Show up and make a plan together.

choices.label: Attend in person
choices.memory: You attended the conference and made a school plan.

choices.label: Schedule a video call
choices.memory: You handled the teacher conference by video.

choices.label: Miss the meeting
choices.memory: You missed the teacher conference and the issue lingered.

baseEvents.title: Bullying Report
baseEvents.description: Your child says another student has been targeting them at school.
baseEvents.wisdom: This is serious. Your child just trusted you with something that scares them. What you do now teaches them whether you have their back. Sometimes you have to be the adult in the room.

choices.label: Meet the principal
choices.memory: You pushed the school for a safety plan after bullying.

choices.label: Coach coping skills
choices.memory: You helped your child practice responses to bullying.

choices.label: Wait and observe
choices.memory: You waited on the bullying report and your child felt alone.

baseEvents.title: Honor Roll Invite
baseEvents.description: The school sends a note: your kid made the honor roll. Your kid is more surprised than you are. Possibly more surprised than their teacher.
baseEvents.wisdom: Your kid worked hard for this. Showing up and making a big deal about it tells them that you see them and that effort matters. This is free emotional fuel for the next hard stretch.

choices.label: Celebrate loudly
choices.memory: You celebrated academic progress and boosted confidence.

choices.label: Quiet congratulations
choices.memory: You gave heartfelt praise for the honor roll invite.

choices.label: Too busy to attend
choices.memory: You missed the honor roll celebration because work ran long.

baseEvents.title: School Play Audition
baseEvents.description: Your child wants to audition for the school play, adding rehearsals to the calendar.

choices.label: Support the audition
choices.memory: You supported the school play audition despite the schedule crunch.

choices.label: Set homework rules
choices.memory: You balanced theater excitement with homework expectations.

choices.label: Say not this time
choices.memory: You passed on the school play to keep evenings simpler.

baseEvents.title: Scholarship Deadline
baseEvents.description: A scholarship application is due this week and could change future school costs.

choices.label: Work on it together
choices.memory: You completed a scholarship application as a team.

choices.label: Hire essay help
choices.memory: You paid for application help and met the scholarship deadline.

choices.label: Let it pass
choices.memory: You missed the scholarship deadline and lost an opportunity.

baseEvents.title: Detention Call
baseEvents.description: The school calls: your child got detention for 'an argument in class.' The details, when they come, are somehow both worse and more understandable than expected.

choices.label: Talk it through
choices.memory: You used detention as a chance to talk through conflict.

choices.label: Strict consequences
choices.memory: You responded to detention with firm consequences.

choices.label: Blame the school
choices.memory: You blamed the school and the conflict escalated.

baseEvents.title: Car Breaks Down
baseEvents.description: The car will not start. Everyone needs to be somewhere. The car does not care.

choices.label: Tow and repair it
choices.memory: You handled a sudden car breakdown with a tow and repair.

choices.label: Use emergency fund
choices.memory: You used savings to keep the car breakdown from taking over the week.

choices.label: Delay and juggle rides
choices.memory: You delayed the repair and spent the week juggling rides.

baseEvents.title: Furnace Goes Out
baseEvents.description: The furnace picks the coldest night of the year to retire. It has made its point.

choices.label: Replace it now
choices.memory: You replaced the furnace before the house got unsafe.

choices.label: Finance the furnace
choices.memory: You financed a furnace replacement to protect cash flow.

choices.label: Patch and wait
choices.memory: You patched the failing furnace and hoped it would last.

baseEvents.title: Tithing Decision
baseEvents.description: Money is tight and the monthly tithe feels harder to justify this month.
baseEvents.wisdom: Generosity practiced in scarcity builds a different character than generosity from abundance. The tithe is as much about who you're becoming as it is about the gift itself.

choices.label: Give the full tithe
choices.memory: You gave the full tithe even during a tight month.

choices.label: Give what you can
choices.memory: You gave a smaller amount with a full heart.

choices.label: Skip this month
choices.memory: You held back the tithe to cover bills.

baseEvents.title: Easter Weekend
baseEvents.description: Easter weekend is here—services, family gatherings, and traditions all collide.
baseEvents.wisdom: The holidays that feel like obligation are the ones you don't invest in. Easter, done intentionally, can be the anchor that kids look back on for decades.

choices.label: Full family Easter
choices.memory: You made Easter a full, meaningful family celebration.

choices.label: Service only
choices.memory: You kept Easter simple with just the church service.

choices.label: Low-key at home
choices.memory: You had a quiet Easter at home with the kids.

baseEvents.title: Christmas Planning
baseEvents.description: It is somehow November and somehow you are not ready. Nobody is ever ready. The decorations are in three different boxes and one of those boxes is missing.
baseEvents.wisdom: Christmas has a way of becoming everything except what it started as. Protecting the meaning of the season from the spending pressure is an active choice, not a default.

choices.label: Set a budget and stick to it
choices.memory: You planned Christmas with a clear budget and kept the meaning intact.

choices.label: Go all out
choices.memory: You went all out for Christmas and loved every moment.

choices.label: Simplify this year
choices.memory: You simplified Christmas and everyone felt the relief.

baseEvents.title: Mission Trip Signup
baseEvents.description: The church is organizing a short-term mission trip and spots are filling fast.
baseEvents.wisdom: Stepping outside your comfort zone in service of others is one of the fastest ways to gain perspective on your own life. These trips change the people who go, not just the people they serve.

choices.label: Sign up and fundraise
choices.memory: You committed to the mission trip and started fundraising.

choices.label: Donate to send someone else
choices.memory: You supported the mission trip financially instead of going.

choices.label: Pass this year
choices.memory: You decided not to join the mission trip this cycle.

baseEvents.title: A Season of Doubt
baseEvents.description: You've been wrestling with questions about faith and haven't told anyone.
baseEvents.wisdom: Doubt that's hidden becomes corrosive. Doubt that's brought into the light—with a pastor, a friend, or a good book—tends to become the foundation of something stronger.

choices.label: Talk to your pastor
choices.memory: You opened up about your doubts and found an honest conversation.

choices.label: Read and journal privately
choices.memory: You worked through doubt quietly through reading and journaling.

choices.label: Keep it to yourself
choices.memory: You kept your doubts bottled up and the weight grew.

baseEvents.title: Unresolved Argument
baseEvents.description: Day two. You both know what started it. Neither of you wants to be the one to say it out loud first.
baseEvents.wisdom: Letting things sit doesn't resolve them—it compounds them. Every day you leave something unaddressed is a day it quietly grows a root.

choices.label: Initiate the conversation
choices.memory: You broke the silence and worked through the conflict.

choices.label: Write a letter first
choices.memory: You wrote out your feelings before talking it through.

choices.label: Let more time pass
choices.memory: You avoided the conversation and the tension grew.

baseEvents.title: Wedding Anniversary
baseEvents.description: Your anniversary is this week. You are only remembering this because of a notification. You will not tell your spouse it was a notification.
baseEvents.wisdom: The years go faster than you think. Marking your anniversary intentionally—even simply—says to your partner that you still choose them.

choices.label: Plan a special dinner
choices.memory: You made your anniversary feel special with a real dinner out.

choices.label: Cook at home together
choices.memory: You cooked a meaningful dinner at home for your anniversary.

choices.label: Forget until it's over
choices.memory: You forgot your anniversary until it was too late.

baseEvents.title: Marriage Counseling
baseEvents.description: A friend recommends a counselor after noticing the strain in your marriage.
baseEvents.wisdom: Going to counseling before things are broken is the smartest use of it. Waiting until the wheels are off is harder on everyone.

choices.label: Book a session together
choices.memory: You and your spouse started marriage counseling.

choices.label: Read a marriage book first
choices.memory: You read a marriage book and started applying the ideas.

choices.label: Dismiss the suggestion
choices.memory: You brushed off the counseling suggestion.

baseEvents.title: Spouse's Hard Week
baseEvents.description: Your spouse has had a brutal week at work and seems depleted.
baseEvents.wisdom: Sometimes the most loving thing you can do is absorb the slack without being asked. Noticing and acting before you're prompted is what makes a partner feel truly seen.

choices.label: Take over the house for the evening
choices.memory: You took over dinner, kids, and dishes so your spouse could rest.

choices.label: Order food and watch a show together
choices.memory: You gave your spouse an easy evening with takeout and a show.

choices.label: Don't notice until too late
choices.memory: You missed your spouse's hard week and they felt invisible.

baseEvents.title: In-Laws Visiting
baseEvents.description: They arrive Friday. They leave Sunday. These are facts you are holding onto.
baseEvents.wisdom: In-law visits rarely go perfectly. Your job is to stay a team with your spouse—that means running interference for each other and debriefing honestly afterwards.

choices.label: Prepare and welcome them
choices.memory: You prepped the house and hosted a good visit with the in-laws.

choices.label: Keep it short and simple
choices.memory: You managed a low-key in-law visit without drama.

choices.label: Let tensions fester
choices.memory: The in-law visit turned into a source of real tension.

baseEvents.title: Spouse Wants a Career Change
baseEvents.description: Your spouse wants to leave their stable job to pursue something more meaningful.
baseEvents.wisdom: Supporting your spouse's growth is part of the long game. Fear is a legitimate input—but it shouldn't be the only one. Talk it through honestly before the resentment of an unanswered dream grows.

choices.label: Discuss a transition plan
choices.memory: You and your spouse mapped out a realistic career transition plan.

choices.label: Express concern but support
choices.memory: You shared your worries honestly and stood behind your spouse.

choices.label: Push back hard
choices.memory: You resisted the career change and damaged trust in the process.

baseEvents.title: Lost Intimacy
baseEvents.description: You realize you and your spouse haven't truly connected in weeks.
baseEvents.wisdom: Intimacy doesn't disappear in one dramatic moment—it fades from a hundred small neglects. Naming the distance is the first step toward closing it.

choices.label: Name it and plan a reconnect
choices.memory: You named the distance and planned a real reconnect.

choices.label: Plan a surprise date
choices.memory: You surprised your spouse with an intentional evening together.

choices.label: Hope it fixes itself
choices.memory: You ignored the distance and the gap quietly widened.

baseEvents.title: Screen Time Battle
baseEvents.description: This is the fourth argument this week about screens. Your child has made compelling legal arguments. None of them are working.
baseEvents.wisdom: Rules without relationship don't work. A screen-time policy that your kids helped create is one they're more likely to follow—and it models the kind of problem-solving you want them to internalize.

choices.label: Create family screen rules together
choices.memory: You created a family screen-time agreement everyone signed.

choices.label: Install parental controls
choices.memory: You set up parental controls and reduced the daily arguments.

choices.label: Keep fighting about it
choices.memory: Screen time stayed a daily battleground.

baseEvents.title: Teenager's Attitude
baseEvents.description: Your teenager has given you the look again. The one that says you are both embarrassing and wrong about everything. You remember being 16. You were also wrong about everything.
baseEvents.wisdom: Teenagers push against the people they're safest with. The dismissal is real but it's usually not personal. Staying curious instead of reactive keeps the door open for the conversations that actually matter.

choices.label: Stay curious and ask questions
choices.memory: You stayed curious about what was behind your teen's attitude.

choices.label: Set clear expectations calmly
choices.memory: You addressed the attitude directly without escalating.

choices.label: Match the energy and escalate
choices.memory: The argument with your teenager blew up.

baseEvents.title: Child's Birthday Party
baseEvents.description: Your child's birthday is coming up and friends are expecting an invitation.
baseEvents.wisdom: The party doesn't have to be Instagram-worthy to be meaningful. You will look at Instagram anyway. You will immediately regret it.

choices.label: Host a real party
choices.memory: You threw a birthday party your child talked about for weeks.

choices.label: Small gathering of close friends
choices.memory: You kept the birthday intimate and meaningful.

choices.label: Low-key family only
choices.memory: You kept the birthday small and easy.

baseEvents.title: Chore System
baseEvents.description: You asked someone to empty the dishwasher three days ago. It has not happened. The dishwasher full of clean dishes is now a philosophical standoff.
baseEvents.wisdom: Kids who have chores learn that belonging to a family means contributing to it. The earlier they learn this, the less jarring the adult world will be.

choices.label: Create a chore chart with consequences
choices.memory: You launched a family chore system that actually stuck.

choices.label: Assign simple daily tasks
choices.memory: You started small with a couple of daily chores each.

choices.label: Keep doing it yourself
choices.memory: You stayed the only one doing housework and burned out.

baseEvents.title: Child Seems Anxious
baseEvents.description: Your child has been withdrawn, tearful, and refusing school. Something feels off.
baseEvents.wisdom: Children show distress in behavior before they can name it in words. The earlier you take it seriously and get support, the less it compounds.

choices.label: Schedule a pediatric evaluation
choices.memory: You got your child evaluated and started the path to support.

choices.label: Talk to the school counselor
choices.memory: You looped in the school counselor and made a plan.

choices.label: Wait and hope it passes
choices.memory: You waited on your child's distress and it grew.

baseEvents.title: Adult Child Moving Out
baseEvents.description: Your oldest is leaving home for the first time and the house will feel different.
baseEvents.wisdom: This is what you raised them for. Pride and grief can coexist. Your job now is to launch them well—not hold on.

choices.label: Help them set up their place
choices.memory: You helped your oldest move out and felt proud doing it.

choices.label: Celebrate the milestone
choices.memory: You marked the launch with a real celebration.

choices.label: Struggle to let go
choices.memory: You had a hard time letting your child go and it showed.

baseEvents.title: Summer Camp Decision
baseEvents.description: Church summer camp registration is open and your child is begging to go.
baseEvents.wisdom: Camp is where a lot of kids encounter something bigger than their parents' faith for the first time. The independence and community it builds is hard to replicate anywhere else.

choices.label: Register for the full week
choices.memory: You sent your child to church camp and they came home changed.

choices.label: Attend a day program
choices.memory: You found a day camp option that worked for the budget.

choices.label: Skip this year
choices.memory: You skipped camp to protect the summer budget.

baseEvents.title: College Conversation
baseEvents.description: Your teenager starts asking serious questions about college and what it costs.
baseEvents.wisdom: The earlier you have an honest conversation about college finances, the fewer surprises land at signing time. Your kid can handle the truth—they just need it early enough to make good choices.

choices.label: Map it out together honestly
choices.memory: You had an honest college planning conversation with your teenager.

choices.label: Start a college savings push
choices.memory: You opened or boosted a college savings account.

choices.label: Avoid the topic for now
choices.memory: You avoided the college money talk and it will cost you later.

baseEvents.title: Aging Parent's Health
baseEvents.description: Your parent's doctor flagged some concerning test results and wants a follow-up.
baseEvents.wisdom: The medical decisions that get made for aging parents often happen fast, under pressure. Being involved and informed now is far better than scrambling later.

choices.label: Attend the appointment with them
choices.memory: You went to the doctor with your parent and advocated for them.

choices.label: Call the doctor yourself for a briefing
choices.memory: You called the doctor to understand your parent's situation.

choices.label: Leave it to your parent to handle
choices.memory: You stayed on the sidelines of your parent's health scare.

baseEvents.title: Parent Shouldn't Drive
baseEvents.description: You've noticed your parent making errors behind the wheel that worry you.
baseEvents.wisdom: This is one of the hardest conversations in eldercare and one of the most important. Driving is tied to identity and independence. Handle it with love and facts, not guilt.

choices.label: Have the honest conversation
choices.memory: You had the difficult driving conversation with your parent.

choices.label: Suggest a driving evaluation
choices.memory: You steered your parent toward a professional driving evaluation.

choices.label: Avoid the topic
choices.memory: You avoided the driving conversation and the risk remained.

baseEvents.title: Nursing Home Decision
baseEvents.description: Your parent can no longer safely live alone and the family needs to make a plan.
baseEvents.wisdom: No decision in eldercare is without grief. The question isn't which option is painless—it's which one best honors your parent's dignity and your family's real capacity to care.

choices.label: Research care facilities together
choices.memory: You led the family through a thoughtful care facility search.

choices.label: Explore moving them in with you
choices.memory: You brought your parent home and took on the caregiving role.

choices.label: Delay the decision
choices.memory: You delayed the care decision and the situation deteriorated.

baseEvents.title: Parent's Loneliness
baseEvents.description: Your widowed parent mentions for the third time this week that they feel alone.
baseEvents.wisdom: Loneliness in older adults is a health crisis, not just a mood. Regular connection—even brief—dramatically changes the trajectory for aging parents.

choices.label: Set up weekly visits
choices.memory: You committed to weekly visits with your lonely parent.

choices.label: Connect them with a senior group
choices.memory: You helped your parent find a senior community group.

choices.label: Send more texts and calls
choices.memory: You increased your digital check-ins with your parent.

baseEvents.title: Sibling Caregiving Dispute
baseEvents.description: You and a sibling disagree over how to handle care for an aging parent—and it's getting personal.
baseEvents.wisdom: Caregiver conflict between siblings is almost universal and almost always about more than the presenting issue. Name the real concern, not just the logistics.

choices.label: Call a family meeting
choices.memory: You called a family meeting and worked toward a caregiving agreement.

choices.label: Bring in a social worker to mediate
choices.memory: You brought in a professional mediator for the caregiving dispute.

choices.label: Let resentment build
choices.memory: The sibling dispute over your parent's care festered without resolution.

baseEvents.title: Power of Attorney
baseEvents.description: Your parent's health is declining and legal documents need to be in order.
baseEvents.wisdom: A power of attorney set up in advance is a gift to everyone involved—especially your parent. Legal clarity during a health crisis is far easier than scrambling after the fact.

choices.label: Consult an elder law attorney
choices.memory: You got the legal documents in order while there was still time.

choices.label: Use an online template
choices.memory: You used a legal template to get basic documents completed.

choices.label: Assume it can wait
choices.memory: You delayed the legal planning and it caused a crisis later.

baseEvents.title: Emergency Fund Gap
baseEvents.description: You realize your emergency fund covers less than one month of expenses.
baseEvents.wisdom: An emergency fund is the difference between a bad week and a financial crisis. Building it slowly and consistently is boring—which is exactly what financial safety is supposed to feel like.

choices.label: Auto-transfer monthly to savings
choices.memory: You automated monthly contributions to rebuild your emergency fund.

choices.label: Cut one expense and redirect it
choices.memory: You found one budget cut and started funneling it into savings.

choices.label: Keep it for later
choices.memory: You acknowledged the gap in your emergency fund and did nothing.

baseEvents.title: Credit Card Balance
baseEvents.description: You've been carrying a credit card balance for six months and the interest is adding up.
baseEvents.wisdom: Credit card interest is a tax on avoidance. The fastest path through it is the one most people resist: pay more than the minimum, every single month, starting now.

choices.label: Start an aggressive paydown plan
choices.memory: You attacked the credit card balance with a focused paydown plan.

choices.label: Transfer to a 0% card
choices.memory: You moved your balance to a lower-rate card and got ahead of it.

choices.label: Keep paying the minimum
choices.memory: You kept paying minimum balances and watched the interest climb.

baseEvents.title: Unexpected Tax Bill
baseEvents.description: The number on the screen is wrong. You check it again. It is still wrong in exactly the same way.
baseEvents.wisdom: Owing taxes isn't a failure—being caught off guard is the problem. This is information to adjust withholding or quarterly payments so next year looks different.

choices.label: Pay it and adjust withholding
choices.memory: You paid the tax bill and corrected your withholding going forward.

choices.label: Set up an installment plan with the IRS
choices.memory: You set up a payment plan with the IRS to manage the bill.

choices.label: Ignore it past the deadline
choices.memory: You ignored the tax bill and faced penalties on top of it.

baseEvents.title: Life Insurance Review
baseEvents.description: You haven't reviewed your life insurance coverage since before the kids were born.
baseEvents.wisdom: Life insurance is an act of love for the people who depend on you. Most people are either underinsured or paying for the wrong thing. A quick review costs nothing and matters enormously.

choices.label: Meet with an advisor
choices.memory: You reviewed your coverage and updated it for where your family is now.

choices.label: Run the numbers yourself
choices.memory: You did a self-audit of your life insurance needs.

choices.label: Put it off again
choices.memory: You postponed the insurance review for another year.

baseEvents.title: Identity Theft Alert
baseEvents.description: A fraud alert appears on your credit card from a retailer you don't recognize.
baseEvents.wisdom: Somewhere, someone is using your card details to buy things you would never buy. This is personally insulting on top of everything else.

choices.label: Freeze credit and dispute immediately
choices.memory: You acted fast on the fraud alert and contained the damage.

choices.label: Call the bank only
choices.memory: You disputed the charge but didn't lock down your credit.

choices.label: Assume it's a false alarm
choices.memory: You ignored the fraud alert and paid a much larger price.

baseEvents.title: Chronic Back Pain
baseEvents.description: The back has been 'a little off' for five months. You have been managing it by not thinking about it. This strategy has stopped working.
baseEvents.wisdom: Chronic pain that goes untreated tends to compound—in your body and in your mood. Most back pain responds well to early, consistent intervention. Waiting makes everything harder.

choices.label: See a physical therapist
choices.memory: You started physical therapy and began recovering.

choices.label: See your GP first
choices.memory: You got a proper diagnosis from your doctor.

choices.label: Manage with painkillers and push through
choices.memory: You masked the pain with medication instead of treating it.

baseEvents.title: Drinking Habits Check
baseEvents.description: You've been reaching for a drink most evenings and it's becoming automatic.
baseEvents.wisdom: Habitual drinking creeps in quietly. If you need it to decompress, that's worth examining—not with shame, but honestly. The habit is usually doing something that a better tool could do instead.

choices.label: Try a dry month
choices.memory: You took a dry month and discovered you didn't need it as much as you thought.

choices.label: Cut back to weekends only
choices.memory: You reduced drinking to weekends and felt the improvement.

choices.label: Keep the current pattern
choices.memory: The nightly habit continued and the effects started to show.

baseEvents.title: Mental Burnout
baseEvents.description: You can't remember the last day you felt rested, motivated, or yourself.
baseEvents.wisdom: Burnout isn't weakness—it's a signal that the output has exceeded the input for too long. Recovery requires intentional rest, not just a long weekend.

choices.label: Take a mental health day
choices.memory: You took a real mental health day and actually rested.

choices.label: Talk to a therapist
choices.memory: You unpacked the burnout with a therapist and started recovering.

choices.label: White-knuckle through it
choices.memory: You pushed through burnout and paid for it on the other side.

baseEvents.title: Preventive Cancer Screening
baseEvents.description: Your doctor recommends a routine cancer screening based on your age.
baseEvents.wisdom: The screenings you skip are the ones that would have caught something early. Early detection is the single biggest factor in cancer outcomes. This is not optional self-care—it's common sense.

choices.label: Schedule it this week
choices.memory: You scheduled and completed your preventive cancer screening.

choices.label: Schedule for next month
choices.memory: You booked the screening for next month.

choices.label: Skip it this year
choices.memory: You skipped the cancer screening and pushed the risk forward.

baseEvents.title: Unexpected Job Offer
baseEvents.description: A recruiter reaches out with an offer that pays more but means relocating.
baseEvents.wisdom: A higher salary is only one variable. Relocation costs, school disruption, and the social capital you'd leave behind are all real. Run the full calculation, not just the number.

choices.label: Negotiate and seriously evaluate
choices.memory: You entered serious negotiations on the job offer.

choices.label: Decline and use it for a raise where you are
choices.memory: You used the competing offer to negotiate a raise at your current job.

choices.label: Decline without exploring
choices.memory: You turned down the offer without fully exploring it.

baseEvents.title: Difficult Coworker
baseEvents.description: There is a person at your workplace who makes everything harder than it needs to be. You are not the only one who has noticed.
baseEvents.wisdom: Difficult coworkers rarely resolve themselves. Addressing it directly—or escalating thoughtfully—is better than absorbing the stress indefinitely.

choices.label: Address it directly with them
choices.memory: You addressed the coworker issue directly and the dynamic shifted.

choices.label: Raise it with your manager
choices.memory: You looped in your manager and a path forward emerged.

choices.label: Suffer quietly and complain at home
choices.memory: You absorbed the coworker toxicity and brought it home with you.

baseEvents.title: Performance Review
baseEvents.description: Your annual review is next week. You have done genuinely good work this year. None of it is written down anywhere.
baseEvents.wisdom: A performance review you're prepared for is an opportunity. One you walk into unprepared is a missed chance to advocate for yourself.

choices.label: Document your wins and prepare
choices.memory: You walked into your review prepared and earned recognition.

choices.label: Ask a mentor to coach you
choices.memory: You got coaching before your review and it showed.

choices.label: Wing it
choices.memory: You went into the review underprepared and it cost you.

baseEvents.title: Layoff Announcement
baseEvents.description: The company announces layoffs and your role may be at risk.
baseEvents.wisdom: A layoff threat is a signal to act, not panic. The people who move fast—updating their network, their resume, their options—are the ones who land best.

choices.label: Update resume and activate your network
choices.memory: You moved fast on the layoff news and put yourself in a strong position.

choices.label: Have an honest conversation with your manager
choices.memory: You got clarity from your manager about where you stood.

choices.label: Hope it doesn't affect you
choices.memory: You did nothing and were caught flat-footed when the layoff came.

baseEvents.title: Work Creeping Into Evenings
baseEvents.description: Your phone buzzed during dinner again. Then during bathtime. Then once more, just to make sure you understood.
baseEvents.wisdom: A boundary that's never enforced isn't a boundary—it's just a preference you announce. Evenings belong to the people who need you most, not whoever sends the last email.

choices.label: Set a hard phone cutoff at 6pm
choices.memory: You set a firm evening boundary and protected family time.

choices.label: Talk to your manager about expectations
choices.memory: You had a clear conversation about after-hours expectations.

choices.label: Keep responding after hours
choices.memory: Work kept taking your evenings and your family felt it.

baseEvents.title: Friend in Crisis
baseEvents.description: A close friend is going through a divorce and calls asking for support.
baseEvents.wisdom: Showing up for a friend in crisis is inconvenient and uncomfortable. It's also one of the most defining things you can do for a friendship. Presence matters more than perfect words.

choices.label: Drop everything and be there
choices.memory: You showed up fully for a friend in crisis.

choices.label: Call and listen for an hour
choices.memory: You gave a friend real time and a listening ear.

choices.label: Send a text saying you're thinking of them
choices.memory: You sent a check-in text but kept your distance.

baseEvents.title: Political Tension at Family Gathering
baseEvents.description: A family dinner turns toward politics and tensions are rising fast. Uncle Gary has opinions. Uncle Gary always has opinions. The mashed potatoes are getting cold.
baseEvents.wisdom: Winning an argument with a family member costs more than the argument is worth. The relationship matters more than the point. You can be right and leave still connected, or you can be right and leave with a fracture.

choices.label: Redirect with curiosity, not combat
choices.memory: You steered the family political conversation away from conflict.

choices.label: Speak your view calmly and briefly
choices.memory: You said your piece without letting it escalate.

choices.label: Engage and dig in
choices.memory: The family dinner became a political argument that damaged the evening.

baseEvents.title: Summer Vacation Planning
baseEvents.description: Summer is approaching and the family wants a vacation—the budget is unclear.
baseEvents.wisdom: A vacation that leaves you in debt isn't a vacation—it's a purchase of future stress. The trip that fits your actual budget almost always becomes the story you tell anyway.

choices.label: Plan a real trip within budget
choices.memory: You took a planned, budgeted family vacation that everyone loved.

choices.label: Road trip to somewhere local
choices.memory: You did a local road trip that punched above its weight.

choices.label: Stay home but plan day trips
choices.memory: You turned the staycation into something worth remembering.

baseEvents.title: School Choice Decision
baseEvents.description: Enrollment season opens for next year and you're considering switching schools.
baseEvents.wisdom: School decisions carry weight but they're rarely permanent. The question to ask isn't just which school is better in theory—but which environment fits your specific child right now.

choices.label: Research and visit both options
choices.memory: You did the research and made a confident school decision.

choices.label: Ask your child's current teacher
choices.memory: You consulted your child's teacher before deciding on enrollment.

choices.label: Default to the same school without looking
choices.memory: You renewed enrollment without researching alternatives.

baseEvents.title: Appliance Breakdown
baseEvents.description: The washing machine has died mid-cycle. Your entire family's clean clothing is inside it, wet, inaccessible, and rapidly becoming an additional problem.
baseEvents.wisdom: An appliance failure always happens at the worst possible time. The decision is usually less about repair vs replace than it is about how quickly you act versus how long you delay.

choices.label: Replace it right away
choices.memory: You replaced the washing machine and got the week back on track.

choices.label: Get a repair quote first
choices.memory: You got the washing machine repaired for far less than replacement.

choices.label: Use the laundromat and delay
choices.memory: You used the laundromat while delaying the appliance decision.

baseEvents.title: Considering a Move
baseEvents.description: A job offer or life change means a possible move to a different city.
baseEvents.wisdom: Moving is among the most disruptive decisions a family can make. The financial upside is only one variable. Schools, community, family proximity, and spouse career impact all deserve equal weight.

choices.label: Visit first and evaluate together
choices.memory: You visited the new city as a family and made a thoughtful decision.

choices.label: Research extensively and weigh all factors
choices.memory: You put real rigor into the relocation decision.

choices.label: Accept on excitement alone
choices.memory: You moved without fully thinking it through and paid the price.

baseEvents.title: Foster Care Inquiry
baseEvents.description: A church announcement about foster care need sparks a real conversation between you and your spouse.
baseEvents.wisdom: Fostering is one of the most demanding and meaningful things a family can do. The call to consider it is worth sitting with seriously—not dismissing, and not rushing.

choices.label: Attend an informational meeting
choices.memory: You went to the foster care info night and began the real conversation.

choices.label: Discuss deeply as a couple
choices.memory: You had a serious, honest conversation about what fostering would mean.

choices.label: Dismiss it as too overwhelming
choices.memory: You closed the conversation before it really opened.

baseEvents.title: Grieving a Loss
baseEvents.description: Someone you love has died and the grief is hitting in waves.
baseEvents.wisdom: Grief doesn't follow a schedule and it doesn't respond to being pushed down. The people who do best are the ones who let it move through them—with support, not in silence.

choices.label: Accept support from your community
choices.memory: You let people in during your grief and didn't carry it alone.

choices.label: See a grief counselor
choices.memory: You got professional support to move through the grief.

choices.label: Isolate and tough it out
choices.memory: You grieved alone and it took a longer, harder toll.

baseEvents.title: Adoption Conversation
baseEvents.description: You and your spouse have been circling the topic of adoption for months.
baseEvents.wisdom: Adoption is one of the most profound things a family can do and one of the most complex. The question isn't whether the impulse is good—it is. The question is whether you go in with full awareness of what it asks of you.

choices.label: Meet with an adoption agency
choices.memory: You took the first concrete step toward adoption together.

choices.label: Read and research deeply first
choices.memory: You spent time researching adoption to approach it honestly.

choices.label: Shelve the conversation for now
choices.memory: You put the adoption conversation on hold indefinitely.

baseEvents.title: Church Conflict
baseEvents.description: A disagreement with church leadership or a fellow member is creating real tension.
baseEvents.wisdom: The church is made of people and people have conflict. How you handle it—with grace and directness rather than gossip and drift—says more about your faith than your attendance record.

choices.label: Address it directly with the person
choices.memory: You handled the church conflict with grace and got to resolution.

choices.label: Pray about it and give it time
choices.memory: You stepped back and gave the conflict space to settle.

choices.label: Quietly pull away from the church
choices.memory: You withdrew from the church rather than working through the conflict.

baseEvents.title: Financial Advisor Meeting
baseEvents.description: A friend suggests seeing a financial advisor but the fees feel unnecessary.
baseEvents.wisdom: Most people are flying blind on retirement and long-term wealth. A fee-only advisor pays for themselves in the decisions they help you make—and avoid.

choices.label: Book a session with a fee-only advisor
choices.memory: You got a real financial plan and felt more in control.

choices.label: Do a free consultation first
choices.memory: You started with a free consultation to test the value.

choices.label: Keep managing it yourself
choices.memory: You stayed self-directed on finances and gaps went unaddressed.

baseEvents.title: Family Meeting
baseEvents.description: You have called a family meeting. The family is immediately suspicious. Someone asks if they are in trouble. Everyone is looking at someone else.
baseEvents.wisdom: Families that meet regularly handle problems before they compound. A recurring family meeting sounds corporate until you see what goes unaddressed in families that don't have one.

choices.label: Call a structured family meeting
choices.memory: You held a family meeting that cleared the air and aligned everyone.

choices.label: Have casual dinner conversations
choices.memory: You opened conversations over dinner and the issues got aired.

choices.label: Keep hoping things sort themselves
choices.memory: The unaddressed issues kept piling up and the tension built.

baseEvents.title: Unexpected Pregnancy
baseEvents.description: A pregnancy test brings news that wasn't in the plan.
baseEvents.wisdom: Life rarely follows the plan exactly. The most important decisions made in this moment are about communication, support, and facing it as a team—not making major choices in isolation.

choices.label: Sit with it together and talk deeply
choices.memory: You and your spouse faced the unexpected news together.

choices.label: Talk to your pastor or counselor first
choices.memory: You sought guidance before making any decisions.

choices.label: React with fear and pull apart
choices.memory: Fear drove you apart at the moment you needed each other most.

baseEvents.title: Job Loss
baseEvents.description: You receive unexpected notice that your position has been eliminated.
baseEvents.wisdom: Losing a job is one of the highest-stress events a family can face—but it's also one of the most revealing ones. How you handle the first week often sets the tone for how long recovery takes.

choices.label: File for benefits and activate network immediately
choices.memory: You acted fast after job loss and built momentum quickly.

choices.label: Take a week to regroup as a family
choices.memory: You took a breath with your family before launching the job search.

choices.label: Panic and isolate
choices.memory: Job loss sent you into isolation and the situation worsened.

baseEvents.title: Water Heater Fails
baseEvents.description: You discover the water heater has died when you step into the shower. The water is a temperature that should not be legal. The repair tech will say 'she's had a good run.'

choices.label: Replace it today
choices.memory: You replaced the water heater before the week got more complicated.

choices.label: Get three quotes first
choices.memory: You shopped quotes and saved money on the water heater replacement.

choices.label: Cold showers for a week
choices.memory: You delayed replacing the water heater and everyone suffered for it.

baseEvents.title: Surprise Medical Bill
baseEvents.description: A bill arrives for a procedure that was supposed to be covered. The bill is for a number that cannot be right. You read it again. It is apparently right. You sit down.
baseEvents.wisdom: Medical billing errors are common. A bill is not a verdict. Calling and asking questions—or hiring a patient advocate—resolves a huge percentage of surprise bills.

choices.label: Call the billing department and negotiate
choices.memory: You challenged the medical bill and got a significant reduction.

choices.label: Set up a payment plan
choices.memory: You arranged a manageable payment plan for the medical bill.

choices.label: Pay it immediately without questioning
choices.memory: You paid the surprise medical bill in full without pushing back.

baseEvents.title: Pipe Bursts
baseEvents.description: A pipe bursts during a cold night and water is spreading through part of the house.

choices.label: Call emergency plumber immediately
choices.memory: You responded fast to the burst pipe and contained the damage.

choices.label: Shut the water and assess damage
choices.memory: You shut off the main valve and managed the pipe emergency methodically.

choices.label: Panic and delay calling
choices.memory: Delayed action on the burst pipe turned a bad situation into a disaster.

baseEvents.title: Sick Child, Work Conflict
baseEvents.description: Your child is sick. Both of you have something important today. The child did not time this strategically but it is hard not to feel that way.
baseEvents.wisdom: In a two-income family, a sick child on a critical work day is a recurring test. The couples who handle it best are the ones who treat it as a shared problem, not a competition over whose day matters more.

choices.label: Divide the day between both parents
choices.memory: You split the sick day fairly and the kid felt taken care of.

choices.label: One parent takes the full day
choices.memory: One parent took the full sick day and covered everything.

choices.label: Send them anyway and hope for the best
choices.memory: You sent the sick child to school and got a call to come pick them up.

baseEvents.title: PTA or School Involvement
baseEvents.description: The school asks for more parent involvement and you've been on the fence.
baseEvents.wisdom: Parental presence in a school sends a message to your child and to their teachers. You don't have to chair a committee—but showing up somewhere is worth more than people realize.

choices.label: Join the PTA and take a role
choices.memory: You joined the PTA and became a presence in your child's school.

choices.label: Volunteer for specific events
choices.memory: You signed up for select school events and it made a difference.

choices.label: Stay uninvolved
choices.memory: You stayed out of school involvement and your child noticed.

baseEvents.title: Retirement Reality Check
baseEvents.description: You open the retirement account for the first time in eight months. You immediately wish you had waited another eight months.
baseEvents.wisdom: Most people are behind on retirement savings and most people do nothing about it. The math gets harder the longer you wait, but the math never gets impossible—until very late. Act now.

choices.label: Max contributions and build a catch-up plan
choices.memory: You faced the retirement gap honestly and started a real catch-up plan.

choices.label: Increase contributions by 2%
choices.memory: You made a small but real move to close the retirement gap.

choices.label: Close the tab and avoid it
choices.memory: You closed the retirement account screen and the gap quietly grew.

baseEvents.title: Parent Remarrying
baseEvents.description: Your widowed or divorced parent announces they're remarrying, and family feelings are mixed.
baseEvents.wisdom: Your parent's new relationship is theirs to have. Your feelings about it are valid. The two things aren't mutually exclusive—and navigating them without poisoning either takes real maturity.

choices.label: Support them and get to know the partner
choices.memory: You chose to support your parent's new relationship with open arms.

choices.label: Express your concerns privately to your parent
choices.memory: You had an honest conversation with your parent about your concerns.

choices.label: Let resentment fester
choices.memory: You let the resentment about your parent's remarriage go unspoken and grow.

baseEvents.title: Pregnancy Loss
baseEvents.description: You and your spouse experience the loss of a pregnancy.
baseEvents.wisdom: Grief after pregnancy loss is real and often private—which makes it heavier. Couples who talk about it, lean on community, and let themselves grieve fully recover their bond. Couples who don't can quietly fracture.

choices.label: Grieve together and lean on your community
choices.memory: You and your spouse grieved together and didn't carry it alone.

choices.label: Seek counseling as a couple
choices.memory: You got professional support after the loss and found your footing together.

choices.label: Shut down and grieve separately
choices.memory: You each grieved alone and the silence created distance.

baseEvents.title: Kids Online Safety
baseEvents.description: You discover your child has been using apps or sites you didn't know about.
baseEvents.wisdom: Kids move faster online than parents can watch. The goal isn't perfect surveillance—it's building the judgment to make good decisions when you're not looking. That starts with a calm, honest conversation.

choices.label: Have an open conversation about online safety
choices.memory: You talked honestly with your child about online safety and trust.

choices.label: Set up parental filters and monitor closely
choices.memory: You updated the tech controls and had the conversation.

choices.label: Remove all devices as punishment
choices.memory: You reacted with removal instead of a real conversation.

generatedEventBlueprints.title: Early Bedtime
generatedEventBlueprints.description: A quiet evening could become actual rest if you protect it.
balanced: You made room for one calm hour.
risky: You scrolled late into the night.

generatedEventBlueprints.title: Urgent Care Choice
generatedEventBlueprints.description: Something is wrong. You cannot tell how wrong. This is the problem with bodies — they are deliberately vague about urgency.
minor: You got timely care for a concerning symptom.
balanced: You used a nurse line to decide next steps.
risky: You waited too long on a concerning symptom.

generatedEventBlueprints.title: Family Emergency
generatedEventBlueprints.description: A relative needs immediate help during a difficult moment.
minor: You showed up for a family emergency.
balanced: You coordinated support for the family emergency.
risky: You stayed out of a family emergency.

generatedEventBlueprints.title: Job Interview
generatedEventBlueprints.description: A strong job lead appears, but preparing will crowd the week.
minor: You prepared hard for a job interview.
balanced: You covered the essentials before the interview.
